title: When does the AdS3 UV logarithm approximate a finite-cutoff length?
question: At fixed ell and L, does the prediction selected in study.json match the numerically integrated bare AdS3 geodesic length at all declared finite cutoffs within 1e-8 length units?

theory.units: x,z,ell,epsilon,L and proper length in one common length unit; logarithm arguments are dimensionless.
assumptions: Endpoints at (+/-ell/2,epsilon), ell=2 and L=1.5 held fixed.
Known-result teaching case, not independent validation of holography.
theory.boundary_conditions: Endpoints at z=epsilon, x=+/-ell/2; epsilon grid in study.json.
theory.observable: Un-subtracted proper length between the two fixed-coordinate-separation cutoff endpoints.
theory.regulator: Finite positive radial cutoff epsilon; no subtraction.
theory.limit_order: All declared cutoffs retained. Only a stated small-epsilon expansion; no extrapolation.
theory.normalization: Proper length L times dimensionless hyperbolic line element; no division by 4G_N.

claim.statement: The selected approximation/comparator matches the finite-cutoff quadrature at the declared accuracy; this is a tested candidate, not a pre-certified truth.
claim.scope: Only the stated fixed-ell geometry, finite grid and accuracy budget.
limitations: Quadrature and antiderivative share the same geodesic geometry.
Simpson estimates are not rigorous error certificates.
Failure of a deliberately tight approximation gate does not invalidate its asymptotic use.
forbidden_inferences: No exact entropy, RT-dictionary proof or new physics.
No agent-effectiveness, safety or generalization claim.

protocol.disconfirming: A model-gate miss with passing integration checks rejects the selected approximation only at the stated finite-grid accuracy budget.
protocol.independence: Adaptive numerical integration vs analytic antiderivative, sharing the prescribed geometry. Tolerance refinement is numerical stability, not an independent derivation.
protocol.failure_interpretation: Non-answer or failed numerical diagnostics stops the walkthrough. A model-gate miss is retained; no failed run is overwritten.
